**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Import the verifier from its sibling directory**

When `database/audit_r1_artifacts.py` is run as documented from this tree, `sys.path` contains the `database` directory, but `ntil_verify.py` is under sibling directory `verifier`; the script therefore immediately raises `ModuleNotFoundError` before auditing anything. Add the sibling verifier directory to the import path or package these modules so the claimed corpus reproduction can actually run.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L10-L10](https://github.com/lijiabao1998/FrontierMath/blob/1cb64019f5e96eb7dac1895b770dc185ceabf3e4/AGENTS.md#L10-L10)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Read the audit corpus from the fetched provenance path**

After the import is repaired (or when `PYTHONPATH` is supplied), this audit still looks for `canonical_evidence/lit_data/known_solutions_1997.txt`, while `fetch_third_party.py` writes it to `canonical_evidence/provenance/known_solutions_1997.txt`. Because there is no corpus-path option, a normal fetched checkout takes the skip branch and ultimately exits 0, so the C3 statement that the corpus portion is reproducible with this script is false and an omitted audit can appear successful.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L10-L10](https://github.com/lijiabao1998/FrontierMath/blob/1cb64019f5e96eb7dac1895b770dc185ceabf3e4/AGENTS.md#L10-L10)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Commit the five retrieval-path cross-check reports**

The cited evidence does not contain the asserted cross-check results: `record_symmetries_ge65.json` only records symmetry analyses, while `all_known_solutions_verification.json` only records aggregate corpus verification; neither contains `paths_agree`, `path_a`/`path_b`, or the claimed per-record `code_sha256` values. Consequently an offline reviewer cannot verify the five identical-point-set claims, and rerunning against the mutable CGI endpoint is not evidence from this same committed tree; commit the five generated JSON reports or narrow this claim.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L10-L10](https://github.com/lijiabao1998/FrontierMath/blob/1cb64019f5e96eb7dac1895b770dc185ceabf3e4/AGENTS.md#L10-L10)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Fail the audit on every failed check**

Fresh evidence after the missing-corpus fix: with a present corpus containing a decode error, this command prints the error but still exits 0, because the return value considers only `missing_corpus`. The same successful exit occurs for corpus verification failures, failed self-certificates, or a vacuous/weak mutation test, so an automated reproduction gate can still report success without reproducing the cited result; derive the exit status from all required audit outcomes and cover them with deliberate failure tests.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L10-L10](https://github.com/lijiabao1998/FrontierMath/blob/553c2075f94203f935c0cd01029e6432da712bc0/AGENTS.md#L10-L10)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve the compared data for offline checking**

Fresh evidence in the newly committed reports shows that they contain only point counts, a hash of path A, empty difference summaries, and the same process's `paths_agree` verdict; they contain neither point set, the coded record, nor the CGI response/hash. An offline reviewer therefore cannot check that the sets are identical and must trust the unrepeatable live-CGI computation, contrary to this sentence; preserve both inputs or decoded sets, or narrow the claim to say only that the reports record the earlier result.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L10-L10](https://github.com/lijiabao1998/FrontierMath/blob/553c2075f94203f935c0cd01029e6432da712bc0/AGENTS.md#L10-L10)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Point default corpus paths at provenance**

After the documented fetch, the corpus is stored under `provenance/dl/`, but this script's default still points to the nonexistent `lit_data/dl/`. Consequently its advertised `python symmetry_probe.py [--json ...]` invocation fails with `FileNotFoundError` unless the caller discovers and supplies `--file`; `cross_check_database.py` has the same stale default at line 99. Use the provenance location so the scripts reproduce against the fetched layout by default.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L10-L10](https://github.com/lijiabao1998/FrontierMath/blob/553c2075f94203f935c0cd01029e6432da712bc0/AGENTS.md#L10-L10)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Include self-certificate failures in the exit gate**

Fresh evidence after `d90aa64` shows the new `reasons` gate still never reads `self_audit["all_pass"]`: when `--r1` contains a certificate that `verify()` rejects, the script prints `all_pass=False` but returns 0 if the corpus checks pass. This leaves one of the audit's advertised inputs able to fail without failing an automated reproduction, so append a reason for failed self-certificates (and preferably for an unexpectedly empty required set).

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L10-L10](https://github.com/lijiabao1998/FrontierMath/blob/d90aa6410a89e2c88c85bdb4f8b3e4f5b9ee4f35/AGENTS.md#L10-L10)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject empty or undecodable database inputs**

When `--file` is empty, or contains only malformed odd-length records such as `abc`, `total == passed == 0` and `decode_errors` remains empty because `decode()` returns `None`; the advertised full-database verifier therefore exits 0 after verifying no configurations. Require every nonblank input line to decode and, outside sample mode, require the expected 431,008 decoded records so a truncated or wrong corpus cannot be certified as successful.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L10-L10](https://github.com/lijiabao1998/FrontierMath/blob/d90aa6410a89e2c88c85bdb4f8b3e4f5b9ee4f35/AGENTS.md#L10-L10)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Regenerate the audit evidence with the current script**

The committed `evidence/r1_artifact_verification.json` cannot have been regenerated by the current script as claimed here: `audit_r1_artifacts.py` unconditionally adds `exit_reasons` before writing JSON, but the committed report ends after `self_certs` and has no such field. Consequently the evidence does not record the new fail-closed gate or its reasons; rerun the current script and commit its output so the artifact is tied to the reviewed implementation.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L10-L10](https://github.com/lijiabao1998/FrontierMath/blob/d90aa6410a89e2c88c85bdb4f8b3e4f5b9ee4f35/AGENTS.md#L10-L10)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Admit this research round before recording results**

This change explicitly records an independent verification and a new attack bench while bypassing `frontier.py start`/`admit`, and the commit adds no `runs/<id>/round.json`. That omits the required base SHA, search/admission evidence, budgets, and retained failure record for this round; create and admit the required round record rather than treating review work as exempt.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L14-L14](https://github.com/lijiabao1998/FrontierMath/blob/bb3bdd883d2ee0bfe3ebf1b97f5d68a8c58214c4/AGENTS.md#L14-L14)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Fail --check when a required source is missing**

When `--check` is set, the outer branch is always entered, but a missing file sets `ok = False` only when `not args.check`; consequently `--check` prints `MISSING` and still exits 0 with “all present and verified.” This is reproducible with `--check --code-inputs-only` when both corpus files are absent, so the documented provenance check can certify sources that were never read.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L8-L8](https://github.com/lijiabao1998/FrontierMath/blob/bb3bdd883d2ee0bfe3ebf1b97f5d68a8c58214c4/AGENTS.md#L8-L8)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Require every collinear triple in the CNF audit**

For a line containing more than three cells, finding one negative triple clause does not establish the required at-most-two constraint, because any other triple on that line may still be selected. For example, retaining only one of the ten diagonal triple clauses in the generated n=5 CNF still makes this function report `covers_all_lines: true`; therefore G2 can approve an underconstrained formula and make a later UNSAT result meaningless.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L12-L12](https://github.com/lijiabao1998/FrontierMath/blob/bb3bdd883d2ee0bfe3ebf1b97f5d68a8c58214c4/AGENTS.md#L12-L12)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Return success only after a proof is checked**

The exit condition is reversed: the current blocked state (`emitted` is nonempty and `with_proof` is empty) returns 0, while provisioning a working pipeline that produces any `SOLVED_WITH_CHECKED_PROOF` result makes the script return 1. Any shell or CI gate using the exit status therefore treats an uncertifiable UNSAT pipeline as successful and the repaired pipeline as failed; base success on the required checked-proof outcome instead.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L12-L12](https://github.com/lijiabao1998/FrontierMath/blob/bb3bdd883d2ee0bfe3ebf1b97f5d68a8c58214c4/AGENTS.md#L12-L12)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject vacuous semantic line audits**

When the DIMACS contains any unrelated contradiction, unit propagation on the entire formula reports a conflict for every assumed triple; the SAT fallback is equally vacuous because it also checks the entire formula. I reproduced this by deleting all ten n=5 diagonal constraints and adding `[1]` and `[-1]`, after which the audit still returned `complete: true`. This can certify a malformed UNSAT instance, so validate the relevant cardinality encoding independently or first establish that the remaining formula is satisfiable.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L12-L12](https://github.com/lijiabao1998/FrontierMath/blob/422bc2a68f6569735bc715fea9976a9d52189b1c/AGENTS.md#L12-L12)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Enforce the frozen A3 acceptance criterion**

The admitted criterion requires every decode-preserving mutation to become illegal, but this gate accepts a 90% rate from at most 400 randomly sampled lines and one random swap per line. Thus a run with known surviving mutations can still pass, and even the recorded `1.0` does not cover every mutation over the 36,912-line corpus, so `all_criteria_passed` does not establish the frozen criterion; either perform the exhaustive check or record A3 as failed and rerun under a prospectively revised criterion.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L10-L10](https://github.com/lijiabao1998/FrontierMath/blob/422bc2a68f6569735bc715fea9976a9d52189b1c/AGENTS.md#L10-L10)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Audit the actual n=75 formula at G2**

Fresh evidence after the earlier completeness finding is that G2 still documents the old “at least one clause” rule and suggests running `benchmark.py`, but that script only calls `negative_controls(5)` and never audits the generated n=75 DIMACS. Following this protocol can therefore mark G2 complete without checking the target formula, and the stated one-clause condition remains insufficient for lines longer than three cells; require the complete audit on the exact hashed n=75 instance.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L12-L12](https://github.com/lijiabao1998/FrontierMath/blob/422bc2a68f6569735bc715fea9976a9d52189b1c/AGENTS.md#L12-L12)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Separate verifier changes from their recorded results**

This commit simultaneously introduces the certificate verifier, regression gates and acceptance thresholds and commits the `ROUND_FINISHED` reports that those new components approve. Marking the round admitted immediately before executing them does not provide the required independently reviewed, frozen verifier/gate boundary; land the verifier and deliberate-break tests first, then execute and record results in a later PR.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L10-L10](https://github.com/lijiabao1998/FrontierMath/blob/422bc2a68f6569735bc715fea9976a9d52189b1c/AGENTS.md#L10-L10)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Audit orbit variables with the orbit mapping**

The documented G2 command generates an orbit formulation, but this call omits `var_of_cell`, so `audit_cnf_covers_lines` assumes that each cell is represented by its row-major variable ID. In `encode_orbits`, cells instead share `y[o]` variables and the weighted line constraints use those orbit IDs; the audit also incorrectly classifies lines according to the cell encoder's explicit/network threshold. Consequently a valid orbit CNF is reported incomplete—I reproduced this with an intact `n=3, group=rot2` instance, where 7 of 8 lines were reported missing—so the required n=75 G2 command cannot validate the target formula.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Avoid solving the target formula as the vacuity guard**

When the target formula is genuinely UNSAT—the outcome this pipeline is meant to investigate—this guard necessarily marks G2 vacuous and incomplete, so the protocol can never proceed to or certify that outcome. It also requires solving the 36-million-clause n=75 instance synchronously before the compute phase, and treats an unchecked solver `False` as sufficient to classify it UNSAT. The guard must instead validate the relevant encoding independently, such as by checking each line gadget in isolation or after removing the target constraints whose satisfiability is under investigation.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L12-L12](https://github.com/lijiabao1998/FrontierMath/blob/b3136028c2ca708fde9c6543731019e87e9db785/AGENTS.md#L12-L12)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Replace the per-line full-DIMACS scan in G2**

For the documented n=75 G2 command, this comprehension scans all 36,418,316 clauses once for each of 1,336,828 maximal lines—about 4.9e13 clause visits before any SAT calls—and the subsequent loop creates still more solver instances. The mandatory pre-compute audit therefore cannot realistically finish within the research budget; index clauses by primary variable once, or directly audit the orbit encoder's explicit pair/triple clauses instead.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L14-L14](https://github.com/lijiabao1998/FrontierMath/blob/d81bfcebad162e7c3ef9b2b2573ba76b7e7da564/AGENTS.md#L14-L14)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject satisfiable but overconstrained orbit formulas**

Local satisfiability does not prevent this semantic check from approving an unrelated stronger constraint: a DIMACS containing only one negative unit `-y_o` for every orbit variable is locally satisfiable with all variables false, makes every violating selection UNSAT, and causes `audit_orbit_cnf(3, ..., "rot2")` to return `complete: true` despite containing none of the intended line gadgets or target-size encoding. Such an overconstrained formula can produce a meaningless UNSAT result, so G2 must verify the intended clauses/equivalence rather than only existence of one local model plus rejection of violations.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L12-L12](https://github.com/lijiabao1998/FrontierMath/blob/d81bfcebad162e7c3ef9b2b2573ba76b7e7da564/AGENTS.md#L12-L12)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Invoke the provisioned independent proof checker**

When a standalone checker is later installed and a solver emits a closing proof, this constant still leaves `independent_checker` false, so `compute_final_status` can never return `SOLVED_WITH_CHECKED_PROOF`. That contradicts the compute protocol's prescribed way to unblock G4 and permanently prevents a genuinely checked pipeline from becoming green; detect and actually run the independent checker, then derive this flag from its result.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L12-L12](https://github.com/lijiabao1998/FrontierMath/blob/d81bfcebad162e7c3ef9b2b2573ba76b7e7da564/AGENTS.md#L12-L12)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Mark the split round execution as not run**

Fresh evidence after the results-splitting fix is that the authoritative `round.json` now says `executed_in_this_pr: false`, and the referenced results directory and `RERUN_EVIDENCE.json` are absent, yet this report still says the round was executed and all A0–A8 criteria passed. This preserves the exact unsupported result claim that splitting was meant to remove; describe these checks as not run until the follow-up commits their evidence.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L14-L14](https://github.com/lijiabao1998/FrontierMath/blob/d81bfcebad162e7c3ef9b2b2573ba76b7e7da564/AGENTS.md#L14-L14)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Build the clause lookup only once**

Fresh evidence after the earlier full-DIMACS-scan finding is that this new containment check rebuilds and sorts a set of all 36,418,316 clauses inside the loop over 1,336,828 lines. Thus the documented n=75 G2 audit still performs roughly 4.9e13 clause visits and cannot realistically finish within the round budget; construct the normalized clause set once before entering the line loop.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L14-L14](https://github.com/lijiabao1998/FrontierMath/blob/9959240df353196bae215d5b10fe88d6e33a027c/AGENTS.md#L14-L14)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject extra constraints beyond the manifested gadgets**

Fresh evidence for the over-constrained-formula issue is that containment only detects missing clauses: a DIMACS consisting of every clause from the genuine per-line manifest plus a negative unit for every orbit variable, while omitting the B3 target-cardinality encoding, still returns `complete: true`. All manifested clauses are present, each local formula is satisfiable with all variables false, and every violation is refuted; because current line gadgets contain no auxiliary variables, the later selectability branch also never runs. Verify the complete expected encoding or otherwise reject such extra constraints before G2 can certify the formula.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L12-L12](https://github.com/lijiabao1998/FrontierMath/blob/9959240df353196bae215d5b10fe88d6e33a027c/AGENTS.md#L12-L12)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Persist the CNF and proof where the parent checks them**

Fresh evidence after the hardcoded-checker finding is that the repaired path remains unreachable when a checker is installed: `run_case` writes only a `.drat` file and never writes the corresponding `.cnf`, while the child writes artifacts beside its temporary JSON rather than in the parent's `json_dir`. Consequently this existence check is always false for newly emitted traces, so the independent checker is never invoked and `SOLVED_WITH_CHECKED_PROOF` remains unattainable.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L12-L12](https://github.com/lijiabao1998/FrontierMath/blob/9959240df353196bae215d5b10fe88d6e33a027c/AGENTS.md#L12-L12)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Require checker success instead of matching `VERIFIED`**

When an independent checker rejects a proof with output such as `s NOT VERIFIED`, this substring test sets `verified` to true even if the checker exits nonzero. I reproduced the resulting `SOLVED_WITH_CHECKED_PROOF` status with a checker returning 1 and printing that message, so a failed proof check can be promoted to certification; require the checker's documented success exit code and an unambiguous positive verdict.

Together with the at-least-one clause emitted above, the control is UNSAT by an immediate contradiction, so C3 passes without exercising the intended pigeonhole/cardinality behavior and the reported `BENCH_SOUND` verdict relies on a broken negative control.
